applet.federation_policy: Read-only projection of one run directory. Data authority stays with the run directory, which is owned by dagrun alone: a host may cache or re-present this document but must not become a second writer. No route writes, claims a node or takes a lease. The server binds loopback only and has no authentication of its own, so a host that presents it to a remote surface is that host's responsibility and needs its own credentialed proxy. Embedding is same-origin by default; a named consumer origin may be allow-listed explicitly, in which case that origin can read this run's titles, statuses and session ids.

mount.notes: Renders this run's nodes and their statuses. No form, no button, no prompt field: every control would be a way to drive an agent from a second surface, which this applet does not offer.

auth.rationale: The server binds 127.0.0.1/::1 only and refuses any other address, so the reachability boundary is the security boundary. There is no token to fake and no write to authorize. A deployment that needs a remote console terminates TLS and authenticates in its own proxy; dagrun stays unauthenticated and loopback.

authority.statement: dagrun owns run.yaml, state.json and trace/. This surface reads them directly and never opens the store, so a monitor cannot sit on the write path. Writing is the `dagrun run`/`claim`/`done` CLI's job, in the run directory, by the process holding it.
